headline: The three standing questions about how this lane works are settled and written into the repo. Finished assembler work now goes up without asking, and the language the game is written in is mine to design with you agreeing to each addition before it lands.
matters: You stop being interrupted for permission to publish work that was already finished, and the other tools stop waiting on you to see it. You start getting a short plain note here whenever I make a design choice that could reasonably have gone the other way. Two things that had been stuck are moving again: the warnings the build has printed since the eighteenth of August, and the padding construct, both of which needed a new word in the language and so had nowhere to go. Neither will be added until you have seen what it looks like.
detail: Decisions d-1, d-2 and d-3 answered by the owner directly; recorded append-only as d-4, d-5 and d-6 per contract/DECISIONS.md rule 8, and banked in docs/OVERSEER.md so a cold boot re-asks none of them. d-1: fast-forward pushes of finished work only, history rewrites still go to him. d-2: deferral grant held, with a notable-call obligation riding on this file rather than a second channel. d-3 answered in his own words rather than by option key, recorded as its own option: propose-discuss-land, sigil owning .emp design, the authored surface going to him before landing, everything behind that surface unilateral. Unblocks WARN-2 and PAD. Contract read at empyrean origin/main 3ca38ac.

headline: The game's source now has a proper way to say "pull this module in, I want none of its names" — the spelling you picked.
matters: Two warnings the build has printed since 18 August were hiding a real one: while those two lines sat there, a genuinely forgotten import in either file would have looked identical and gone unnoticed. The game's own files change next, on the engine side, and then the warnings go away for good.
detail: WARN-2. `use base._` merged at 4e262006, master e36debf8, pushed. Owner chose it over a `require` keyword and an @allow opt-out. `_` stays an ordinary identifier; reserved by name at `use` and `module` headers so one spelling never carries two meanings. Byte-identity proven red-first against a reached module that emits; nothing under golden/, pins.rs or repin.toml moved. Aeon adoption deliberately not done (sequencing). CORPUS_OPEN_FINDINGS rows kept and re-pointed at adoption.

headline: The assembler's test suite is not green against the current engine, and it has not been for a while.
matters: Five checks fail because the engine declares a piece of the game into a slot its own layout file deliberately leaves empty. Nothing I changed caused it and no amount of refreezing clears it. It matters because the nightly check that is supposed to catch exactly this does not watch those five, so it has been reporting all-clear every morning over a red suite. I have told the engine lane.
detail: 3844/5/4 against aeon master 415e0b6a, reconciling exactly (3853 declared). Reproduced on unmodified sigil master bc05f446 in a detached worktree, same AEON_DIR — that control is what separates pre-existing from parcel-caused. Cause verified in aeon: effects_scenes.emp declares module ...ojz_effects_editor_act1 while map.toml carries the block as RESERVED SLOT with no row. None of the five is in SOURCE_GATES.

headline: Adding content no longer bricks the build: sections are placed from the map's order and their real sizes, and the old frozen table only warns.
matters: When a level, object or background band grows, the build now moves its neighbours and prints a warning naming the section and by how much, instead of failing with no way to regenerate the tables. Every shipped ROM is byte-for-byte unchanged today. One background band can now be built; the engine lane runs the single refreeze that proves it on the real scene.

CRCs s4 c7b9d10d/699106, s4.debug f0175028/715010, demo c708b114/96336, demo.debug dec88cc1/101044 identical before/after at clean aeon 415e0b6a, equal to provenance tip. Suite 3852/5/4 (3861 declared, reconciles), same five pre-existing failures by name, 0 skip lines, clippy exit 0. Merged tree's crates/ identical to the tested commit (master had moved by docs only). Red-first: 4 of 6 unit tests and both integration tests shown failing under deliberate breaks. Open: SECTION-ROW, CLOSURE-FIX, REPIN-END, FIVE-REG, Option B step 3 (declared quantum), aeon's real-band build + refreeze + bganim_room.py retirement.

matters: The engine lane stops hand-editing a label per scene save; a reserved slot can be declared before it has any content and just works the day it does. Shipped ROMs are unchanged, and the check that proves it accepts either spelling, so the engine's switch-over cannot break my suite.

matters: Every red check of the last week is accounted for and fixed, none by loosening a check. The last one was a test that built its map from a hand-kept list instead of the real one; that list can never learn a content-named section, so the check was moved onto the real build and the dead path is booked for removal.

headline: The nightly check now builds every shipped ROM from source each morning and says out loud how many checks it skipped, so a broken build cannot hide behind an all-clear.
matters: Honest correction to what I told you on the 24th: last week's red checks were mostly my own test rigs, not something the nightly could ever have seen, and the one real build break lived only in uncommitted engine files. What is new is that a committed break is now caught the next morning by name, and the nightly can no longer report green while silently skipping most of its checks. It also caught a gate that would have taken the nightly dark tonight.

headline: The three red checks are green again, and a kind of silent rot in the test rigs is closed rather than patched.
matters: The rig that builds Sonic's file kept two hand-written lists of what that file needs. Both had drifted without anything noticing: one had never learned about the insta-shield you just added, and the other still named three things from when Sonic's file held code it no longer has. A wrong entry there links cleanly, so no check could ever catch it. Both lists are now read from the file itself. Separately, when a value lands in the wrong kind of field the error now points at that field instead of at the whole record, which is the thing that made the engine lane chase the wrong field last week.

Part 1: compile_sonic takes the act-descriptor closure via native_section; sonic_extern_names derives the outbound seam from the module's own extern("...") calls, addressed via listing_symbol_addr on the shape's sibling .lst, replacing pins::* hand-pins that had rotted in both directions (stale Perform_DPLC/Draw_Sprite/Ability_None, missing Ability_InstaShield). Design call ratified: the act-descriptor precedent's 'independent authority' was nominal, since the old seam read pins::* which repin regenerates from the same build's listing; the dedicated drift alarm repin_pins::pins_rs_is_current survives untouched, and rings_port.rs:364 already used listing_symbol_addr. Ledgered: 16 unconverted with_ambient rigs (36 sites), the define-matrix rigs that cannot slice a whole-program build, and the missing sigil-ir API for enumerating a section's unresolved refs (which would catch a stale pin too).

headline: The padding construct you said yes to is built and shipped, and three error messages that no test protected now have tests.
matters: You can now write the offset you actually want and let the compiler work out the filler, instead of hand-counting a number that silently goes wrong the moment anything above it changes. The old hand-counted spelling still works where the count is genuinely what you meant, and warns with the exact replacement line when it looks like a mistake. Nothing in the game moved a single byte. Separately, and less comfortably: my own instructions sent the agent at the wrong reference copy of the engine, because a note in my docs listed checksums that this morning's refreeze had moved and nothing can keep a number in prose current. It cost the agent a wasted run, it caught it itself, and I have replaced those numbers with a command that derives them.
